meta.methodology_note: First run of this module (v2.1). The reference file with exact scoring weights (references/treasury-auctions.md) was not present in the bundled skill this run, so absorption_score / dealer_stress_score use a documented first-pass methodology: absorption_score = 30%*(100-dealer_pctile) + 30%*indirect_pctile + 20%*btc_pctile + 20%*direct_pctile, weighted 60/40 toward the most recent vs second-most-recent settled auction; dealer_stress_score = 40%*dealer_pctile + 30%*(100-btc_pctile) + 30%*funding_stress_term (from SOFR-IORB spread). tail_bps left null per instructions (no reliable free when-issued yield source). Recommend formalizing exact weights in the reference file for future runs.

treasury_auctions.narrative: The Treasury Auction module is live for the first time this run. Both auctions that settled this week — Tuesday's 2-Year and Wednesday's 5-Year Note — cleared cleanly: dealer take sat in the 25th-35th percentile of the trailing 20 comparable auctions (well below levels that would signal dealers being forced to absorb unwanted supply), and NY Fed's primary-dealer net Treasury inventory has been declining for three straight weekly prints. SOFR is trading 1bp below IORB, a textbook-normal funding reading with no repo stress. None of the three transmission flags (auction weakness, dealer pressure, repo confirmation) are triggered. This reads as 'duration repricing' territory if yields do move — not 'Treasury intermediation stress.' Today's own 7-Year Note auction hasn't settled yet and will be the next real test of this read.
